To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the tidal charges of a black hole are not only a function of the black hole mass and the brane tension, but also of the bulk scalar field.

(1) for a given value of tidal charge the entropy of a scalar quantum field is larger in the brane world than in the bulk and (2) the entropy is larger for a larger value of tidal charge, which means that the entropy increases as the brane world is pushed further away from the bulk.

(i) the tidal charge of a BWBH can be either positive or negative depending on the values of the parameters of the model and the sign of the bulk cosmological constant, and (ii) the entropy of the scalar field in the presence of the tidal charge is either positive or negative, depending on the sign of the tidal charge, and the values of parameters of the model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the thermodynamics of black holes in the brane world scenario.
the study of the thermodynamic and the quantum statistical properties of the Schwarzschild black holes (BH) in the context of the brane world scenario.
the study of the properties of the scalar field in the black hole background.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the semiclassical calculation of entropy for a scalar field in a brane world black hole is not possible in the presence of the 5D tidal charge.
the semiclassical entropy of scalar field is a monotonically decreasing function of the brick wall cutoff, which is the inverse of the brick wall radius.
the semiclassical calculation of scalar field entropy in the background of brane world Schwarzschild black holes with tidal charge is in good agreement with the Bekenstein-Hawking area law.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in the case of extreme tidal charge, the scalar field entropy is found to be independent of the brick wall cutoff.

the entropy of a scalar in the BWBH background is not a universal function of the brick wall cutoff, but rather a universal function of a new parameter, which is a combination of the tidal charge and the brick wall cutoff.
the semiclassical scalar field entropy is a function of the brick wall cutoff, tidal charge and the brane tension.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the semiclassical entropy is a function of both the brick wall radius and the tidal charge.
the semiclassical entropy of the field, S, in the BWBH background is a function of the brick wall cutoff, the tidal charge, and the mass of the black hole.
in the extreme tidal charge regime the entropy is dominated by the contribution of the scalar field in the near horizon region.
